description: The misleading-name half of the policy. The change adds a grace window (real logic, explained by a comment that earns its line) and, in the same edit, makes `isSessionValid` write `lastChecked` on every call. An `is` predicate that mutates its argument is the shape a reader will not predict from the name: every caller that calls it twice, or calls it from a read path, now has a side effect nobody at the call site can see. The grace comment and the new `remainingMs` are must-not-flag: one is documentation that earns its line, the other is a well-named pure function.

evidence_trace: src/auth/session.ts:12 keeps the name `isSessionValid` and the boolean return
src/auth/session.ts:14 adds `session.lastChecked = now;`, a write to the argument
src/auth/metrics.ts:4 filters sessions with isSessionValid while computing countValidSessions, and the adjacent grace-window comment does not expose mutation
finding.failure_scenario: A dev adding session-validity checks to a read-only metrics sweep can expect isSessionValid to leave sessions unchanged, but the boolean predicate also updates lastChecked.
finding.model_authored_prose: `isSessionValid = (session: Session, now = Date.now()): boolean` (session.ts:12) now writes `session.lastChecked = now` (line 14). countValidSessions filters with this predicate (metrics.ts:4), and the adjacent grace-window comment explains expiry tolerance, not mutation. Rename it to checkAndRecordSession so a dev adding a read-only validity check can see that this operation is not a pure predicate. Renaming preserves the grace window and timestamp recording without splitting their behavior.

prContext.title: auth: tolerate a 30s grace window on session expiry
prContext.description: Requests that raced the session expiry were failing on their last hop. Sessions now validate for 30 seconds past expiresAt, and the check records when it last ran. Adds remainingMs for the client-side countdown.
